From advancing the methodologies underpinning two key publications – the Access to Medicine Index and the Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Benchmark – to publishing two reports via our Diabetes Care Programme, the Foundation continued to provide actionable insights to guide industry efforts in expanding access to life-saving medicines worldwide.

Report: Lancet Global Health Commission on Medical Oxygen Security - Over 5 billion people lack medical oxygen access: urgent action needed

description.narrative: A staggering 5 billion people—over 60% of the world's population—lack access to safe, affordable medical oxygen services, according to the newly released report by the Lancet Global Health Commission on Medical Oxygen Security​. The report sheds light on a hidden but deadly crisis, where millions of preventable deaths occur each year due to conditions like pneumonia, stroke, and surgical complications—all requiring oxygen therapy.

Report: Access to diabetes care for children and young people: Pharma companies' current actions and opportunities ahead

description.narrative: As rates of type 1 diabetes (T1D) rise among children and young people (CYP), so does the urgency to establish reliable access to lifesaving diabetes care products in underserved regions. By analysing company-backed diabetes care initiatives aimed exclusively at supporting CYP living with T1D, this report from the Foundation’s Diabetes Care Programme sets out practical solutions for scaling access for CYP in low- and middle-income countries.

G&BM Programme expansion

description.narrative: Building on the first Generic & Biosimilar Manufacturers (G&BM) Programme report published in 2023, work in 2025 concentrated on defining the scope of the Programme’s second phase. In addition to five G&BM companies from the initial report (Cipla, Hikma, Sun Pharma, Teva, and Viatris), the Foundation identified additional Africa-based companies for inclusion in the G&BM Programme (Aspen, Emzor, EVA Pharma, Sothema, Universal Corporation Ltd). In 2026, a report will be published to showcase how the companies in scope are approaching supply and availability in African countries for a range of essential medicines.

Podcast: Advancing women’s health through inclusive innovation

description.narrative: In this episode of The Health Equity podcast, Jayasree K. Iyer, CEO of the Access to Medicine Foundation, speaks with Andrea Lucard, formerly Chief Officer of Corporate Strategy and Affairs at Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV).As part of the Health Equity through Her Lens campaign, they explore how inclusive innovation can help close persistent gender gaps in healthcare. Andrea shares lessons from her leadership at MMV, the Concept Foundation and Women in Global Health, highlighting how research, partnerships and policy must evolve to better serve women and girls. From tackling malaria in pregnancy to improving representation in global health leadership, this conversation dives into the systemic change needed to make healthcare more equitable and responsive to the needs of women and girls worldwide.

description.narrative: In this episode of The Health Equity podcast, Jayasree K. Iyer, CEO of the Access to Medicine Foundation, speaks with Dr Boitumelo Semete-Makokotlela, CEO of the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA).The conversation focuses on the evolving role of regulators in expanding access to medicine across Africa. Dr Semete-Makokotlela discusses how public-private partnerships are unlocking new solutions and why trust, capacity and collaboration are key to getting life-saving products to patients faster. She explains why regulation is becoming part of broader health system conversations and what pharmaceutical companies should understand about engaging with African markets.

description.narrative: In this episode of The Health Equity podcast, Jayasree K. Iyer, CEO of the Access to Medicine Foundation, speaks with Dr Jerome Kim, Director General of the International Vaccine Institute (IVI).They discuss what it takes to make equitable access to vaccines a global reality, why major pharmaceutical companies often overlook diseases affecting low- and middle-income countries and how new partnerships and regional manufacturing initiatives are reshaping the vaccine landscape.The conversation explores the growing movement for vaccine security, the importance of long-term investment in local capabilities and how innovation and collaboration can help bridge persistent gaps in access.

Podcast: Bridging the gap - Insights from the 2024 Access to Medicine Index

description.narrative: In this episode of The Health Equity podcast, Jayasree K. Iyer, CEO of the Access to Medicine Foundation, speaks with Dr Joseph Saba, CEO of Axios International, about how pharmaceutical companies are addressing access challenges and the role of measurement in driving progress. Drawing on insights from the 2024 Access to Medicine Index, they discuss what it takes to translate commitments into action in low- and middle-income countries.Dr Saba shares insights from decades of experience, from the early days of the HIV/AIDS response to today’s evolving landscape of global health. The conversation highlights key access strategies, the importance of collaboration and what more needs to be done to ensure that life-saving medicines reach the people who need them most. With global health funding under increasing pressure, they also discuss what this means for pharmaceutical companies working to expand access. As the funding landscape shifts, companies and other stakeholders must find new ways to adapt and sustain progress.

Podcast: The role of lived experience in driving global health equity

description.narrative: In this episode of The Health Equity podcast, Jayasree K. Iyer, CEO of the Access to Medicine Foundation, speaks with Florence Riako Anam, Co-Executive Director at the Global Network of People Living with HIV (GNP+).Florence shares her personal journey as a woman living with HIV and discusses how people with lived experience are helping reshape global health policies and access strategies. She explains how patient advocates are driving change by participating in high-level decision-making and what lessons from HIV advocacy can be applied to other disease areas. The conversation explores how the pharmaceutical industry, governments and communities can collaborate more effectively to expand access to healthcare in low- and middle-income countries.

Podcast: The role of responsible investment in expanding access to medicines

description.narrative: In this episode of The Health Equity podcast, Jayasree K. Iyer, CEO of the Access to Medicine Foundation, speaks with Rogier Snijdewind, Senior Director Active Ownership at PGGM.They explore the crucial role of responsible investment in expanding access to essential medicines in low- and middle-income countries. Rogier shares how PGGM integrates healthcare access into its investment strategy and how investors use the Access to Medicine Index to engage pharmaceutical companies. Together, they discuss key metrics investors track, examples of successful and challenging engagement and why responsible investment is a powerful tool for driving sustainable access to medicines globally.

2025 Investor engagement

description.narrative: Investor Engagement team held the Investor briefing , a series offered company-specific analysis from the Index and created space for more focused discussion on priority access-to-medicine issues. These exchanges with lead and signatory investors helped identify practical ways investors can support progress on global health equity and encourage stronger company performance. Throughout the year, the team engaged investors on the 2024 Index’s findings and recommendations, supporting investor action to drive improved access to medicine and responsible industry practices. In February, the Foundation hosted the SDG3 Collaborative kick-off call that brought together nearly 60 investors – the highest participation to date – for an in-depth review of the 2024 Access to Medicine Index. Quarterly SDG3 Collaborative meetings also took place online, with lead investors sharing updates from their engagements with pharmaceutical companies. To help investors apply Index insights in their stewardship and engagement activities, we provided targeted resources and practical support throughout the year. This included ongoing access to our investor toolkit – featuring FAQs on the Index methodology, common questions raised in investor discussions and company specific meeting note templates with context on past engagements and key topics of interest – as well as Investor Briefings on each company featured in the Index.
